item.title: How supervisors keep police training alive after the academy
item.description: The academy lays the foundation, but strong supervisors turn training into lasting performance

item.title: Building strong leaders starts at the first supervisory level
item.description: While leadership challenges can emerge at any level, they most often take root at the first supervisory level, where decisions, attitudes and accountability shape everything that follows

item.title: ICE hits back at Boston, says police ignored 167 detainer requests in 2025, not 57
item.description: Acting ICE director Todd Lyons said many requests involved assault, weapons and drug charges

item.title: Wash. ranks last in nation for officers per capita as hiring struggles continue
item.description: The state added 68 officers in 2025, but population growth outpaced hiring, further lowering staffing levels, Washington Association of Sheriffs and Police Chiefs data shows

item.title: Sheriff: Fla. deputy shot ‘dead center,’ survives 6-foot shootout after BWC takes hit
item.description: The Volusia County deputy was working with a trainee on his eighth day of patrol when a suspect opened fire; despite being wounded, he broadcast suspect details before being rushed to a trauma center

item.title: BWC: Calif. sergeant shot in head during gunfight with carjacking suspect
item.description: After being shot in the hand, the San Jose sergeant returned fire before a second round struck him in the head

item.title: Texas DA calls officers ‘heroes,’ denies prosecution rumors after Austin mass shooting
item.description: Travis County District Attorney José Garza said his office is not seeking charges against the officers who fatally shot a gunman during a downtown mass shooting
